summary_hint: borrower(s), property, lender, closing date, loan amount / rate / APR, total closing costs and cash-to-close, and whether this is the final or a corrected CD — the headline a processor wants without opening the five-page disclosure.

encoding_variations: Cash-to-close appears twice: the 'Calculating Cash to Close' table (page 3) and the borrower transaction-summary bottom line (page 3, Section K−L). Same fact; capture the disclosed cash_to_close total and note which page.
'To Borrower' vs 'From Borrower' — cash-to-close carries a direction; a sign flip inverts AS-3. Capture the sign/direction, not just the magnitude.

Fee 'paid by' columns — Borrower-Paid At Closing / Before Closing, Seller-Paid, Paid by Others, (Lender credits) — a fee's tolerance bucket depends on who paid; each line item needs its paid_by column as its disambiguator.
Final vs Corrected CD — the same fee set can appear on multiple CDs; final_or_corrected_indicator plus disbursement_date distinguish the operative version.
APR vs interest rate — the CD states both; do not read the note rate for DC-5.

open_questions.q: cd_delivery_or_received_date derivability (DC-3). The 3-business-day clock runs from the date the borrower received the CD, which many CDs do not print.
options: add the field and accept frequent nulls
treat DC-3 as reading a delivery timestamp from the LOS/e-sign audit trail, not this document
open_questions.recommendation: keep the field (marked absent-from-catalog) so the AI captures it when present, and flag to the rule author that the authoritative source is likely the delivery log, not the PDF.

open_questions.q: One combined line-item list vs two (loan costs A–D and other costs E–J). Combined here with a section discriminator.
options: one combined list with a section discriminator
two lists split by loan-costs vs other-costs
open_questions.recommendation: keep combined — DC-4 needs every fee regardless of section, and one list is one plumbing site. GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Tolerance bucket is derived, not printed. The CD does not label fees '0%' or '10%'; closing_cost_line_items carries section + paid_by and DC-4 derives the bucket. Do not invent a bucket field.
options: carry section + paid_by and let DC-4 derive the bucket
open_questions.recommendation: confirm DC-4's mapping from section → bucket lives in the rule, not the schema.

open_questions.q: Second nested list for the cash-to-close summary? AS-3 could benefit from the page-3 transaction-summary lines (deposit, adjustments, payoffs) rather than flattened totals.
open_questions.recommendation: start with flattened totals; add a transaction_summary_lines list only if AS-3's author needs line-level detail. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Degraded percent/bool/enum types. apr, interest_rate (percent), loan_purpose, final_or_corrected_indicator (enum) all degrade to str (no coercer).
open_questions.recommendation: accept str now; consider a percent coercer if DC-5 arithmetic proves fragile against string rates.

notes: Scope note: only AS-3 is NOW/IN. CL-3 and CL-6 are BLOCKED/OUT (post-close), and DC-3/DC-4/DC-5 are SCOPE?. The fields each rule will read are still derived so the schema is ready when scope is confirmed. CL-6 has no field consumer so it is absent from rules_served.
No existing_extractor for this document — no diff section; all fields exists_today false.

This is the CFPB/TRID Closing Disclosure, a fixed 5-page form (page 1 Loan Terms + Projected Payments; page 2 Closing Cost Details A–J; page 3 Calculating Cash to Close + Summaries of Transactions K–N; page 4 loan disclosures; page 5 Loan Calculations + contacts). Closing-cost sections: A Origination, B/C Services (B cannot-shop = 0% tolerance, C can-shop = 10% bucket), E Taxes/Recording, F Prepaids, G Escrow, H Other. The A/B vs C distinction drives DC-4.

PII section flags borrower_name, borrower_name_2, borrower_names_raw, seller_name (person names, pre_masked false), property_address (real address, pre_masked false), and loan_number (confidential, pre_masked true) for _PII_FIELDS registration; person names use an invented kind 'NAME'.
